rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before real data; synthetic validation at real counts in five periods (noise bias, two invalid selection tests and the persistence null found and handled as amendments A1-A5); 33 replication periods with both embedding models; three natives (NE29, NE32, #51 growth); 712 estimate rows; frozen, guarded confirm script dry-run, not run. No holdout run, no parent-offspring (heritability) test, no cross-boundary split.
rationale.faithfulness: The partition is an exact identity on all 247 transitions and its cross-fitted shares are unbiased at real counts. The HH's content and selection clauses hold everywhere (transmission 0.98 in 33/33; |selection| 0.01). The style clause holds only as an ordering (style migration > content in 21/26 periods with turnover), not as dominance (0/33). The egregore reading fails (C > 0 in 0/29). Selection is not identifiable and copying is not separable from a field at day resolution. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A monitor can read within-period content shifts as day fields acting on stayers, not as influence or composition, and treat style shifts on roster days as mostly composition (style migration share ~10x content's). The implied day-field fractions (style 0.07, content 0.32) are a gauge. It gives no lever and cannot detect copying.

one_line: Village content changes by transmission (share 0.98, 33/33 periods), selection is undetectable (0.01), style moves by migration more than content (21/26) but still mostly by transmission; no attractor (C > 0 in 0/29).

models.note: Price split: transmission dominates; selection undetectable; style partly migration
No differential-influence selection beyond the permutation null
Neutral null realised as the fitness permutation
